newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Anti-Kabila march in Congo diamond town - residents.
newsitem.headline: Anti-Kabila march in Congo diamond town - residents.

text.p: Demonstrators denouncing the new government formed by Laurent Kabila marched in the streets of the Democratic Republic of Congo's diamond mining centre of Mbuji-Mayi on Friday, residents said on Saturday.
They said by telephone that Friday's protest was triggered by the exclusion from the government of veteran politician Etienne Tshisekedi, who comes from Kasai and has a huge following there.
"There were lots of people demonstrating and troops fired into the air to disperse them," said one resident. The exact number of demonstrators was unclear.
The city was calm on Saturday with businesses open.
A week ago Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL) entered the capital Kinshasa after long-serving president Mobutu Sese Seko fled.
In naming a new government, Kabila abolished the post of prime minister, which Tshisekedi claims for himself on the basis of a 1992 national conference although he was sacked by Mobutu.
Kabila's troops on Friday fired shots in the air in the capital Kinshasa to turn back a demonstration by a few hundred of Tshisekedi's supporters.
Tshisekedi was the most stubborn political opponent of Mobutu and has a strong following in Kasai and Kinshasa.

Mbuji-Mayi is home to the MIBA diamond mine, producing largely industrial-grade stones, which since the collapse of revenues from copper and cobalt mines in the early 1990s has become the state's main export revenue earner.
